method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC) 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)' (published 6 August 2021). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © Elsevier Ltd (author manuscript; no open licence stated on the PMC page, which shows only the PMC copyright notice) (read at PMC article page 'Copyright and License information' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. AI-USE CLAUSE (recorded per owner decision, not used to exclude): the Lancet site-wide footer reads "All content on this site: Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd., its licensors, and contributors. Text taken from the PMC author manuscript; figures and supplementary appendix not used.

claims.claim: **Get tissue whenever possible:** histopathology with fungal stains (such as Grocott methenamine silver) plus fungal culture. Blood cultures pick up only about half of cases in advanced HIV.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Histoplasma antigen in urine or serum** gives a rapid probable diagnosis and can be followed over time. Serology helps most in chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis and may fail in severe immunosuppression.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exposure history matters:** the fungus lives in soil contaminated by bat and bird droppings; it is highly endemic in the Mississippi, Ohio and St Lawrence basins and common in Latin America, but occurs worldwide, including Africa and Europe.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Moderate-to-severe disease in advanced HIV: induction with liposomal amphotericin B,** which improved survival over the deoxycholate form in a randomised trial (3 mg/kg daily). Other amphotericin formulations are acceptable if the liposomal form is unavailable.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After induction for disseminated disease, give itraconazole 200 mg twice daily, usually for at least a year.** Itraconazole alone is an alternative induction option for less severe infection.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prefer itraconazole to fluconazole** for milder disease: fluconazole works less often and resistance can emerge on it. Voriconazole is not routinely recommended.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In people without immunosuppression, treat for at least 6 months,** adjusting for severity and site.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Histoplasmosis on a TNF-alpha inhibitor: stop the TNF blocker during antifungal treatment.** Immunosuppression may be restarted after a clinical response, about 12 months of antifungal therapy and a negative Histoplasma antigen.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnose by culture and histopathology of skin or tissue aspirates or biopsies;** culture is the most sensitive test but can be negative, and histopathology is often negative. Imaging is rarely needed unless spread to bone or deeper tissue is suspected.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Species matters:** *S. schenckii* usually causes chronic subcutaneous disease, whereas zoonotic *S. brasiliensis* (spreading from Brazil) often causes more severe infection.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cutaneous and lymphocutaneous disease: itraconazole 200 mg orally once daily, continued for 2–4 weeks after the lesions resolve** (typically 3–6 months in total). Response rates with itraconazole are 80–100%.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatives: terbinafine 500 mg orally twice daily, or itraconazole increased to 200 mg twice daily.** Do not use voriconazole or isavuconazole, which appear ineffective. Potassium iodide works but is poorly tolerated.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Disseminated or severe pulmonary sporotrichosis: liposomal amphotericin B 3–5 mg/kg daily (or deoxycholate amphotericin 0·7–1·0 mg/kg daily), then step down to itraconazole 200 mg twice daily for at least 12 months** once the patient is improving.
claims.locator: European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and ISHAM, The Lancet Infectious Diseases (NIH author manuscript in PMC), 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of the endemic mycoses: an initiative of the European Confederation of Medical Mycology in cooperation with the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (Thompson GR 3rd et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021;21:e364-e374)', published 6 August 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450022/, retrieved 2026-09-23
